sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text:
Nanta Tech is a rapidly expanding AV integrator and technology reseller moving into robotics, AI services and Robot-as-a -Service. The reported growth is substantial, but cash conversion and the return on newly deployed capital are not yet consistent with a durable compounder. BQS is 4.7/10. GQS is 5.0/10 after a weak-cash ceiling, versus raw 5.75. IAS is NS, not a mid-range score, because current price, funding and execution data are insufficient.

The central risk is that growth consumes capital before shareholders receive cash. FY26 revenue reached ₹70.10 crore and profit ₹8.17 crore, while operations consumed ₹10.01 crore and cash capex used ₹20.24 crore. The audited March cash balance includes ₹0.80 crore of unspent IPO earmarks, leaving only ₹0.33 crore available for other uses. Receivables rose to ₹39.99 crore. This is not evidence of a current default: the examined audits report no default, and management subsequently described substantial collections.

Classification: Hold — unresolved. Preserve it in a separate SME research cohort, excluded from actionable investment rankings until funding and tradability gates are resolved. It is not an evidence-backed compounder. At an expressly assumed ₹338.40, the funded base scenario produces about 14.2% annualized return, slightly below the 15% hurdle, and requires hypothetical equity funding. A cheaper quotation alone would not fix cash discipline.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 factors are GOV5, MOAT4, REV8, DUR5, CAP4, CASH2, BAL4, EXEC5, EARN5, with R/D/P/L all NS. Every factor retains supporting facts, contrary evidence and source IDs. REV uses the common growth schedule and a short-history ceiling; it receives no bonus for an AI theme, prospective contracts or low quoted multiples.

BQS =.20×5 +.20×4 +.12×8 +.10×5 +.12×4 +.10×2 +.08×4 +.08×5 =4.66, displayed 4.7. GQS =.40×8 +.20×5 +.15×5 +.15×4 +.10×2 =5.75. CASH2 reflects persistent poor realization and triggers the explicit final GQS ceiling 5.0. These are separate business and growth-quality views, not two scores to add together.

IAS reuses unrounded BQS4.66 exactly: its known contribution is.25×4.66 =1.165. With missing weight.75 and no neutral imputation, the mathematical bound is 1.915–8.665, not a forecast, a midpoint or an actionable ranking. Coverage is 25%. The point score remains NS. The independent gates override any possible classification matrix cell. One-point factor sensitivities retain the exact weights; no hidden discretion is added after scoring.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Nanta sells and integrates AV equipment for enterprises, education, hospitality and other customers. It sources displays, conferencing equipment and associated hardware, combines them into solutions, and supports installation and service. It also sells branded Allbotix service robots and builds software/AI solutions. The economic model is therefore a mixture of distribution, projects, engineering and emerging recurring services, not a demonstrated pure-software platform.

FY25 disclosed revenue was ₹38.87 crore from AV integration, ₹2.44 crore from AV products, ₹5.46 crore from robots and ₹4.47 crore from software. FY26 audited goods sales fell from ₹46.78 crore to ₹42.92 crore while domestic services rose from ₹4.46 crore to ₹26.18 crore; export services added ₹1.01 crore. Outsourced software consultancy, technical/social-media work, telecom and cybersecurity expenses became material. Segment-specific gross margins, retention, installed-base utilization and recurring-versus-project service revenue are not separately demonstrated.

The original MNT proprietorship business was transferred in February 2024. RSVP’s business undertaking was acquired in late March 2026. A wholly owned UAE subsidiary and 51%-owned TRN research subsidiary were created in April 2026, after the standalone FY26 closing balance sheet. Their expansion costs must not be confused with proven incremental profit. Retained ownership of RaaS robots means that customers’ zero-upfront-capex offer shifts capital requirements to Nanta.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest plausible advantage is practical integration capability: a customer can buy equipment, customization, installation and maintenance from one supplier. Dealer relationships, a functioning service network and software integration can create modest switching costs once deployed. None of these facts alone establishes durable pricing power. The prospectus explicitly describes sourcing without long-term supplier contracts and competition on price, quality, durability and execution.

FY25 top 10 customers represented 91.95% of revenue and top 10 suppliers 95.91% of purchases. Dealer customers explain part of the concentration, but that explanation does not diversify credit risk. H1 FY26 top 10 customer concentration fell to 67.30%, a genuine positive. The July Aimtron MOU preserves Nanta design/IP ownership and supports an asset-light manufacturing route; it does not independently establish patents, manufacturing cost leadership or recurring software economics.

PRO FX provides the closest listed AV distribution/integration comparison. Its FY26 operations also consumed ₹10.17 crore despite ₹15.17 crore PAT, showing that sector growth need not generate cash. Purple Wave is a commercial AV integration comparator with older FY25 cash realization of only ₹0.71 crore on ₹9.12 crore PAT. Kody is adjacent in robotics/software, but other income and standalone/subsidiary scope differ. None justifies transferring a SaaS multiple to Nanta. MOAT4 reflects useful, contestable capabilities rather than no business value.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
The preferred comparable history begins with FY23 MNT predecessor revenue ₹9.5572 crore. FY24 combines the predecessor operating period with Nanta after the business transfer, giving ₹26.5962 crore rather than treating legal incorporation as new organic demand. FY25 and FY26 revenue were ₹51.2356 crore and ₹70.1037 crore. The three-year CAGR is 94.3%; latest annual growth is 36.8%. Five comparable financial years are unavailable, so the starting REV9 is capped at 8. No extra small-base adjustment is applied after using the correct operating lineage.

FY26 growth is qualitatively less uniform than the headline: goods declined, services expanded sharply, and gross-versus-net exposure to outsourced delivery is not separately quantified. The audited acquisition note presents RSVP historical revenue ₹20.5121 crore without a contribution period. Management said the late March transaction contributed almost nothing to FY26. It would therefore be wrong to subtract all ₹20.5121 crore from FY26 and call the residual organic. Conversely, adding RSVP’s FY27 target ₹15–20 crore to future sales is acquisition growth and is modeled separately.

The scale remains small and customer-concentrated. Four hundred-plus robots sold is a management claim supporting a commercial footprint, not evidence of a large installed subscription base. No audited price/volume bridge, renewal cohort or future market-share forecast is assumed.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Demand access is better evidenced than durable self-funding. The ₹6.60 crore Pointers Insurance AI order is a specific six-month customer contract. The Connplex LOI describes 100 robots at ₹40,000 per robot per month for 36 months, implying ₹14.40 crore over the entire deployment term and a ₹4.80 crore annual run-rate at full rollout. It remains subject to definitive MSA/POs and deployment timing. The Aimtron ₹10 crore figure is prospective manufacturing purchases by Nanta, not customer revenue or an additional order book.

Normalized NOPAT is operating EBIT after a 25.17% assumed tax. FY24–FY26 incremental NOPAT of ₹5.37 crore divided by incremental invested capital ₹47.29 crore yields 11.4%. Removing the late March RSVP consideration from ending capital gives 11.6%; latest FY25–FY26 incremental return is 9.3%. These aggregate bridges support CAP4 against an explicitly assumed 12–16% capital-cost range, without requiring private project cohorts. They do not establish matured returns for the recent office/software buildout.

GQS is capped at 5 because profit growth has not converted into cash. A credible upgrade needs collections, repeat customer demand and operating returns on the fresh capital, not just higher sales. The model separates acquired revenue, continues recurring R&D after initial budgets expire, and funds working capital and replacement capex. UAE and TRN assets are not assigned additional standalone values on top of operating enterprise value.

sections.title: Management Governance and Execution
sections.text:
The September 30 filing shows promoter ownership 57.50% and no reported pledge. Founder-family ownership can align interests and concentrate decision-making; it is not by itself either a moat or misconduct. FY26 actual related purchases were approximately ₹0.50 crore from Nozti and ₹0.003 crore from MNT. Directors supplied interest-free loans, with ₹0.87 crore outstanding. The AGM’s much larger proposed RPT ceilings are permissions, not actual transfers; future use deserves monitoring.

The finance-leadership change effective 29 May 2026 warrants attention during rapid scaling. Main audits, CARO and IFC reports are unmodified on the reviewed matters. The IPO utilization cover states full use while the detailed table/certificate retains ₹0.7964 crore; the detailed number is used because it agrees with the annual report. This inconsistency is a disclosure-quality concern, not evidence that proceeds were diverted.

Execution positives include the successful IPO, revenue expansion, completed RSVP undertaking purchase, new subsidiaries and specific new orders. The counterweight is incomplete evidence that the experience-centre investment and RaaS rollout generate cash returns. The proposed 625000 warrants and authorized 500000 ESOP options can expand shares substantially; approval is not a receipt or grant. The valuation report’s regulatory floor ₹384.21 is based largely on past market VWAP, not a guarantee of intrinsic value or a protected share price.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 CFO was −₹10.0113 crore. The reconstructed cash bridge starts with PBT ₹11.0072 crore, adds D&A ₹0.4855 crore, interest ₹0.1093 crore and gratuity ₹0.0100 crore, then subtracts the ₹0.0893 crore FX gain to reach ₹11.5227 crore before working capital. The source displays the gain with a positive sign; this is an analyst arithmetic correction, not a claimed source amendment. Receivables consumed ₹19.1103 crore, inventory ₹2.2204 crore, advances ₹4.0059 crore and other assets ₹1.1959 crore, partly funded by ₹6.2581 crore payables and ₹0.6924 crore other liabilities. After ₹1.9520 crore cash tax, CFO matches. CFO+ CFI+ CFF reconciles closing CFE ₹1.1267 crore within rounding.

FY24–FY26 combined CFO is ₹-10.68 crore versus PAT ₹15.44 crore, a -69.1% realization ratio. FY26 free cash flow after cash capex is −₹30.2471 crore. Closing receivable days are 208 versus average-balance days 158; the two measures are not interchangeable. ₹5.5062 crore is beyond six months overdue and no impairment allowance is recorded. A 10% loss of March receivables would absorb ₹4.00 crore, roughly 49% of FY26 PAT, before tax effects.

The original versus IPO-restated profits are explicitly reconciled in the prospectus. In particular, H1 FY26 restatement adds ₹0.2185 crore MSME interest. Latest FY26 comparatives return to original audited figures; one must not splice bases and invent a profitability trend. The FY26 MSME interest table shows zero without a separate continuity bridge. Standard balance-confirmation caveats remain relevant to the large debtors/advances/payables. The auditor did not report a bank-return discrepancy: the <=₹5 crore working-capital facility exemption makes that test not applicable.

Large late FY26 software/server additions of ₹6.6301 crore and a 10 year amortization policy explain why reported D&A may understate a mature annual replacement charge. The scenario uses explicit depreciation and recurring R&D rather than capitalizing all growth costs. The old tax provision and credits are separated and paid once in the cash bridge; the already completed RSVP acquisition is not paid a second time. The FY26 ratio note shows ROE0.06, whereas PAT divided by simple average FY25/FY26 equity is 25.48%; ending-equity ROE is 16.35%. The discrepancy is retained, not silently quoted as a verified 6% ratio. Average-capital ROCE is likewise sensitive to the late IPO, while closing-capital and incremental-return bridges give the more demanding capital test. Clean audit opinions are preserved alongside these economic reservations.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
No authenticated 19 October historical close was retained. ₹338.40 is explicitly an assumed scenario entry price, inspired by dated labels on secondary rolling pages, not a verified cutoff quotation. At that assumption and 5130170 shares, equity value is ₹173.60 crore, current-share FY26 EPS ₹15.93, P/E21.25 times and P/B3.47 times. The weighted reported EPS ₹20.20 is not the current-share EPS. FY25 ending-share EPS ₹12.7079 to FY26₹15.9260 grew 25.3%, versus PAT growth 74.5% and weighted EPS growth 56.5% (₹12.91 to ₹20.20). Excluding other income after an assumed 25.17% tax gives FY26 current-share EPS ₹15.76; this limited operating adjustment does not normalize future D&A, R&D or credit costs. Combining assumed equity value with March debt and unearmarked cash gives an illustrative EV/operating EBITDA of 15.45 times; it is not a synchronized current EV.

The model runs from March 31 balances through exact 20 October 2031, splitting the 20 October 2026 entry date and funding events. FY27 legacy revenue grows 5/15/25% in bear/base/bull and separate acquired RSVP sales start at ₹10/15/20 crore. Margins before separately expensed R&D are 12/18/22%; receivable days 220/180/135; recurring capex 5/4/4% of sales. Exit EBITDA multiples 8/12/16 are analyst scenarios, not validated peer quotes. Capital needs, old taxes, debt repayment assumptions, operating cash reserve and reinvestment continue through the horizon. No post-terminal proceeds or double-counted property value are included.

Under the 15 day reserve, none of the no-new-funding core paths is feasible. Even the base zero-reserve sensitivity has a funding gap of ₹2.56 crore under its explicit collection/tax assumptions. These are modeled gaps, not observed default. Ordinary and non-rescue conditional returns are suppressed where any required floor is breached, including before entry. A separate third-party equity rescue assumes 20% discount to the assumed price and 2% fees, rounded up to whole shares. It requires ₹22.87/₹5.89/₹3.45 crore net in bear/base/bull and produces -20.2%/14.2%/40.8% annualized assumed-price returns. The base 15% hurdle entry price is ₹327.02, conditional on that rescue, not an actionable buy price.

Pre-entry rescue paths are counterfactual funding diagnostics, not descriptions of what occurred. They change shares before the entry date, whereas the observed 30 September filing still has 5130170 shares. They must not be treated as a current-entry funded forecast or proof that capital was received. A usable current-entry valuation must reanchor cash, obligations and actual shares to authenticated current public evidence. The proposed warrants are optional. Conditional receipts are dated 1 November 2026 and 30 April 2028 solely for stress testing; warrants-only paths cannot repair earlier cash troughs. ESOP stress includes 500000 shares and minimum ₹10 exercise proceeds. Genuine growth×multiple and reserve×DSO×capex surfaces, plus 12/15/18% hurdles and verified finite reverse-growth brackets, are embedded. Return factor R and price-implied factor P remain NS until actual current inputs are established. Transaction costs/market impact are not reliably measurable; a separate implementation haircut is provided rather than assumed zero execution risk.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent Loss Path
sections.text:
Permanent-loss risk is High. The linked failure path is project delays or service concentration, slower collections, supplier/debt/tax payments that cannot wait, and repeated equity funding at discounted prices. A quoted drawdown alone is not this mechanism. If receivables prove collectible and growth costs are restrained, funding pressure can be transient; if not, existing shareholders bear dilution or impaired earning power.

The explicit rescue bear assumes 5% legacy growth, ₹10 crore acquired sales with no subsequent growth, 12% margin before recurring R&D, 220 day receivables and 5% capex. It needs ₹22.87 crore net equity and ends at ₹109.57 per share versus assumed ₹338.40, a -67.6% terminal price change. This is after modeled rescue, not evidence that investors would actually provide that funding. Without rescue, returns are not presented as executable.

A 10% receivable impairment is ₹4.00 crore; faster software obsolescence, ₹5 crore R&D rather than ₹2–3 crore, or failure to convert the Connplex LOI would make economics worse. Low booked debt does not protect against taxes, aged creditors and working capital uses. Operating property could support recovery but is not marked up or added twice to the valuation. Losses remain borne by common shareholders after senior claims; no arbitrary probability is assigned to the severe path.

sections.title: Five Times and Ten Times Feasibility
sections.text:
Five-times and ten-times wealth over 1826 days require approximately 37.98% and 58.50% annualized returns respectively, before personal tax and execution cost. At assumed ₹338.40, terminal share prices are ₹1692 and ₹3384. One must solve share-level wealth after funding and dilution, not multiply enterprise value or management sales targets.

The funded bull scenario reaches ₹1873.33 per share, about 5.54 times, but needs simultaneous 25% organic growth, successful acquired sales, 22% pre-R&D margin, 135 day collections, disciplined capex and 16 times exit EBITDA. It is an upside combination, not the base thesis. The funded base reaches only 1.94 times. The base-economics reverse search for five/ten-times wealth tests−10% to 80% organic growth with 12 times exit multiple, carrying all rescue dilution; neither goal crosses within that tested range, so no endpoint is mislabeled as the required growth solution.

The practical bottleneck is not an asserted national TAM. It is funding customer credit, deploying retained RaaS hardware, paying software development and proving repeat economics without surrendering the upside through dilution. The five-times possibility under a much stronger bull mix does not qualify Nanta as an evidence-backed compounder; current quality, cash and funding gates fall short. Ten-times is not supported by a credible demonstrated path.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before any implementation decision, obtain the next published half-year/full-year cash flow and a dated reconciliation of unrestricted cash, IPO earmarks, utilized CC, tax payments and subsequent financing. A warrant allotment or receipt filing must establish timing, amount and actual shares, not merely approval. Compare actual cash collections against new invoicing; do not count gross collection announcements as free cash.

Operating checkpoints: confirm the Pointers Insurance project acceptance/collection; distinguish signed Connplex MSA/POs and live paid robots from the original LOI; establish capex per robot, downtime, monthly fees, renewals and maintenance cost. For Aimtron, track delivered manufacturing POs and cash terms, not the indicative ₹10 crore headline as sales. Disclose RSVP revenue and profit contribution separately to protect organic comparability. For UAE/TRN, distinguish external spend, intragroup funding, minority interests and recurring R&D from new earnings.

Thesis upgrade thresholds are at least two reporting periods of positive operating cash with a credible reduction in receivable days/aged balances, audited returns on fresh capital above the 12–16% assumed capital-cost range, and funded growth without repeated surprise dilution. Thesis deterioration includes mounting overdue balances, new audit qualifications, unpaid statutory dues/default notices, unexplained related-party transfers or capitalized costs without cash returns. Retrieve an actual BSE20/60 session window, current lot/restriction status and bid-ask depth before evaluating the ₹5 lakh reference. Normal price volatility alone changes valuation, not business quality.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification is Hold — unresolved, with mixed business quality and cash-constrained growth. The financial research is sufficiently substantial to identify operating and capital risks, but it is not an actionable current-price assessment. G3 and G4 exclusions control ranking flags. Numeric BQS/GQS can be shown transparently in an excluded-by-gate SME research list, not silently mixed into investable main-board rankings or assigned a neutral IAS.

Conditional action is to keep the name on an evidence-led watchlist and reassess after public cash/funding and market execution evidence improve. Do not recommend a trade, leverage, or a suitable position from the illustrative ₹500,000 test. At the assumed price, one 600 share lot costs ₹203,040; a ₹500,000 budget buys at most 1200 shares for ₹406,080, while 1800 shares costs ₹609,120 and exceeds it. Neither arithmetic capacity nor a market maker establishes availability, spread or ability to exit.

A confirmed funding receipt alone would not resolve poor incremental capital returns, and a lower multiple alone would not establish a moat. Conversely, negative CFO during expansion is not automatic fraud or proved insolvency. The classification should change only when the relevant gates and economics change, using the same framework and disclosed score rules.

The source register retains issuer/exchange URLs, payload hashes and document page references. Core primary evidence is the full FY26 annual report; scanned FY24/FY25 reports including audit annexures; December 2025 prospectus with restated financials; May 2026 IPO utilization certificate; June 5 earnings call; specific acquisition/order/MOU/LOI filings; September ownership; and the PCS/warrant valuation documents. Facts, management statements and analyst assumptions are labeled in the evidence register. Key assumptions include the ₹338.40 scenario price, 15 day cash reserve, 25.17% tax, 12–16% capital-cost range, explicit debt repayment dates, future margin/collection/capex paths, hypothesized equity rescue and optional warrant/ESOP timing. Exact dates, funded brackets and all annual/scenario/sensitivity rows are available with the report. summary:
Nanta Tech is a rapidly expanding AV integrator and technology reseller moving into robotics, AI services and Robot-as-a -Service. The reported growth is substantial, but cash conversion and the return on newly deployed capital are not yet consistent with a durable compounder. BQS is 4.7/10. GQS is 5.0/10 after a weak-cash ceiling, versus raw 5.75. IAS is NS, not a mid-range score, because current price, funding and execution data are insufficient.

The central risk is that growth consumes capital before shareholders receive cash. FY26 revenue reached ₹70.10 crore and profit ₹8.17 crore, while operations consumed ₹10.01 crore and cash capex used ₹20.24 crore. The audited March cash balance includes ₹0.80 crore of unspent IPO earmarks, leaving only ₹0.33 crore available for other uses. Receivables rose to ₹39.99 crore. This is not evidence of a current default: the examined audits report no default, and management subsequently described substantial collections.

Classification: Hold — unresolved. Preserve it in a separate SME research cohort, excluded from actionable investment rankings until funding and tradability gates are resolved. It is not an evidence-backed compounder. At an expressly assumed ₹338.40, the funded base scenario produces about 14.2% annualized return, slightly below the 15% hurdle, and requires hypothetical equity funding. A cheaper quotation alone would not fix cash discipline.
